# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 55 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 55 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_055_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 5, Part 1 — The Vineyard Parable Begins

**55:1** "Hear," he said, "the parable that I am about to tell you, as it relates to fasting. A certain man had a field and many slaves. And he planted in a certain part of the field a vine, and he appointed a certain slave as steward, trustworthy and well-regarded, and gave him the vineyard to fence it around, and commanded him: do nothing more to the vineyard until I come, but keep this commandment of mine, and you shall be free in my house."

**55:2** "And the master of that slave went away to a foreign country. So when he had gone away, that slave took and fenced the vineyard, and when he had finished fencing the vineyard, he saw that the vineyard was full of weeds."

**55:3** "So he reasoned within himself, saying: I have carried out the lord's commandment — I will now also dig this vineyard, and it shall be more beautiful when it is dug; and being free from weeds it shall give more fruit, not being choked by the weeds. So he dug and cleared all the weeds out of the vineyard. And that vineyard became very beautiful and flourishing, not being choked by weeds."

**55:4** "After some time the master of that slave and of the field came, and he entered into the vineyard and saw that the vineyard was beautifully fenced and also dug, and all the weeds pulled up, and the vine flourishing. He rejoiced greatly at what the slave had done, and called his beloved son and his friends who were his counselors, and told them what he had commanded the slave and what he had found to have been done."

**55:5** "And they rejoiced with the master because of the slave. And he said to them: I promised this slave freedom if he kept my commandment which I gave him. He has kept my commandment and has also done a good work for the vineyard, and has pleased me greatly. In return for this work which he has done, I wish to make him joint heir with my son, because when he had a good thought, he did not neglect it but carried it out."

**55:6** "The master's son agreed with this decision, that the slave should be made joint heir with the son. After some days the master made a feast and sent him many foods from the feast. When the slave received the foods that were sent to him by the master, he took enough for himself and distributed the rest to his fellow slaves."

**55:7** "His fellow slaves rejoiced as they received the foods, and began to pray on his behalf, that he might find even more favor before the master, because he had acted so toward them. All these things his master heard and rejoiced greatly at his actions and at the goodness of his heart. So the master called together his friends and his son and reported to them how the slave had acted with the foods that he had received; and they were even more pleased that the slave had been judged worthy of the joint inheritance with the son."

---

*EMET renders the Greek of P.Mich. 130 with maximal literalness, preserving the vineyard parable of Similitude 5 which bears christological significance.*
